purpose: Describe a fresh allocation diagnostic for the frozen owner-row-fusion build. This diagnostic reports sampled allocation evidence only; it does not test superiority, release readiness, or an allocation pass gate.

requirements: Verify all six pilot page bytes, lifecycle checks, five served production asset hashes, COOP/COEP headers, and the v5 Chromium engine tuple.
Verify the exact five production asset bytes against the frozen source/build inventory before accepting either arm.

collection.profileScope: Whole page from about:blank through product import, mount, 60 warmup frames, 240 measured frames, correctness inspection, and disposal.
collection.order: Serial, in the listed order; each page uses a fresh headed context, GPU disabled, and 1200x900 viewport.

limitations: There is one pair at each size, so these profiles are diagnostic rather than a release allocation gate.
Sampling is probabilistic. The profile covers the whole page and should not be read as per-update allocation cost.
Post-disposal heap readings are not mounted-cache measurements or universal leak proof; JavaScript heap excludes DOM, GPU, and presentation memory.
Allocation evidence does not establish CPU speed, causal improvement over historical candidates, independent-device performance, or a general advantage over React.

prohibitions: Do not edit frozen source, build, protocol, correctness pilot, or timing evidence.
Do not launch a server, navigate to product pages, or collect profiles during planning or verification preparation.
Preserve failures and raw profile trees/samples; do not rerun selected pages or exclude observations.
Verify the archive union, all three checkpoint maps, correctness pilot, V5 diagnostic, served bytes, exact six-page sequence, raw allocation samples, excerpt offsets, and post-locks independently.
